newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission moots revamp of air traffic body.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission moots revamp of air traffic body.

text.p: Europe's air safety organisation Eurocontrol should be revamped to separate its various functions and to give it the muscle to enforce decisions intended to reduce delays and ease congestion, the European Commision said on Wednesday.

"The organisation of air traffic management is a major factor in flight delays and one of the cost burdens on air carriers that the Commission is pledged to reduce," the EU executive said in a statement.
"The Commission is proposing that Eurocontrol should be reformed (so) as to separate its regulatory and operational functions," the statement said.

"It should be made responsible for the regulation of various security aspects, the formulation of air traffic management policy, procedures and norms, as well as the regulation of civilian air space."

Commissioners agreed at their weekly meeting a mandate for the EU to negotiate membership of Eurocontrol, the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation, so that EU-level concerns would be represented directly during the body's meetings.

Eurocontrol was set up in 1960 to provide air traffic control in the air space of its members, who now number 22 European countries including the EU's 15 members less Finland and Spain. Decisions are taken on the basis of consensus and without a mechanism for ensuring implementation.

Operations at Eurocontrol include running a computerised flow control management system which coordinates flight plans submitted by member countries so as to make the most of available air traffic control capacity.

Atilla Parla, director of the secretariat at Eurocontrol's Brussels-based executive, said it was too early to comment on the Commission proposals, which in any case require EU member state approval before they go any further.
